rv.q: Irene Macdougall is a fabulously unknowable O’Brien, and Jessica Hardwick brings grit and humour to Julia, Winston’s famously underwritten love interest, although the pair share barely a spark of chemistry.

Guided by Emily Jane Boyle’s sharp movement direction, the ensemble convincingly captures the rigid, uneasy rhythm of a population under constant scrutiny. Despite the suffocating dread, the production grips the room so completely that looking away is never an option.
Competent adaptation of George Orwell’s dystopian novel
The audience was thoroughly gripped throughout, even in spite of the less than cheerful themes of the story.

There’s a magnificent sense of coming full circle in reviewing any staging of George Orwell’s 1984 . Writing a piece where readers engage with and share an independent opinion on a creative work is a privilege many of us take for granted.
